caption: A tennis ball is tossed straight up in a backyard and comes back down to the same spot.

sa.check: A tennis ball is tossed straight up in a backyard.
It rises and then comes back down.
It comes down to the spot it went up from.
The toss goes straight up rather than off to one side.
The rise comes first and the fall follows.

pc.expect: The ball slows as it rises, hangs for an instant at the top, and falls quicker and quicker on the way back down.
pc.fail: The ball climbs at an unchanging speed all the way to the top; or it stays at the top instead of coming back; or it goes quicker the higher it rises.

pc.expect: It comes down along nearly the line it went up and lands near the spot it left.
pc.fail: The ball comes down well away from where it went up with nothing pushing it aside; or it curves off to one side in the open air; or it keeps rising out of the frame and never returns.

pc.expect: Once in the air nothing but the fall changes the ball's motion.
pc.fail: The ball jinks sideways in mid-air with nothing touching it; or it halts in mid-flight and hangs there; or it sets off again after coming to rest on the ground.

pc.expect: The ball stays round and firm, squashing only briefly where it lands.
pc.fail: The ball stretches as it flies; or it stays flattened after landing; or it wobbles like jelly in the air.

pc.expect: One ball is in the air throughout and it stays above the ground.
pc.fail: The ball vanishes at the top of its flight or a second one appears; or it passes through the ground; or it turns into another object in mid-air.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The ball's colour, the yard and the background stay the same.
pc.fail: The ball changes colour in flight; or the fence or wall behind changes between frames; or the yard rearranges.
